prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D layout of a gear room as the camera wearer turns from an aisle between a left whiteboard wall and a right ski rack (frames 1–3) toward an open doorway on the right (frames 4–5). In frames 1–3, bright regions show the left wall and right partition/handrail within arm's reach (~0.3–0.6 m), a floor backpack below to the left at ~1–1.5 m, and the ski rack at ~0.5–1.5 m, while in frames 4–5 the wearer approaches the doorway frame (~1.5–2 m away) with shelving to the right (~1.5–3 m) and a person standing before an elevator in the dark background (~3.5–4 m in frame 4, narrowing to ~2.5–3.5 m in frame 5). The person stands ~0.5 m to the left of a ski/bag rack (within that person's arm's reach) and faces forward toward the camera wearer, partially occluded by the doorway edges. Compared to the motion-blurred RGB in frames 2–3, the depth map clearly separates the foreground partition wall, doorway frame, and recessed elevator alcove. However, it is unreliable on fine structures like individual skis and wire shelving, which merge into smooth blobs, and it flattens the distant person and elevator into near-uniform dark tones.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and background instances against an unlabelled black background, detecting the floor backpack on the lower left in frame 1 (~1.5 m away) and the standing person in the doorway in frames 4–5 (~2.5–4 m away). In frames 4–5, the person mask grows and shifts slightly right as the camera wearer approaches and turns toward the doorway, showing the person standing upright, facing and looking toward the camera wearer, with their head and feet slightly clipped in frame 4. While segmentation cleanly outlines the distant person's silhouette in the dim elevator alcove where dark clothing blends into the background in RGB, it provides no geometry for the surrounding walls, doorway, or shelving within the wearer's arm's reach (~0.3–0.8 m). The map is highly unreliable on clutter and motion blur: in frame 1 it falsely labels blue gear and a yellow boot on the upper-left rack (~2.5–3 m away) as two overlapping 'person' instances, in frames 2–3 it misses the backpack and all scene objects entirely, and in frame 5 it misclassifies the dark bags on the rack (~0.5 m to the right of the person, within the person's arm's reach) as a second 'person'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the sequence, rendering only a single vertical yellow body-keypoint cluster in the left-center of frame 2 and no magenta hand skeletons in any frame. In the RGB strip, the only actual person in view stands in front of the elevator in frames 4 and 5 (~2.5–4 m in front of the camera wearer, facing and looking toward the wearer with arms hanging down near a gear rack within their arm's reach at ~0.5 m), while walls and racks lie within the camera wearer's arm's reach (~0.3–0.8 m) on the left and right. Because no valid skeletons are detected in frames 4–5, the pose map contributes no useful spatial information beyond what is visible in the RGB frames and fails to track the person's approach, facing direction, or limb positions. Furthermore, it is unreliable in frame 2, where it hallucinates a compact vertical body skeleton on the dark backpack and gear lying on the floor (~1–1.5 m below and to the left of the camera wearer), and it completely misses the real person in frames 4 and 5.
